bib.title: USR: An Unsupervised and Reference Free Evaluation Metric for Dialog Generation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 681-707

question: Can an unsupervised, reference-free metric built from RoBERTa sub-metrics correlate with human judgement of open-domain dialog responses better than word-overlap and embedding metrics?
hypothesis: Reference-free sub-metrics for specific dialog qualities, combined by a regression, correlate with human quality ratings better than reference-based metrics because dialog is one-to-many.
contributions: a strongly-correlated, unsupervised and reference free metric is proposed for evaluating open-domain dialog systems
a thorough human quality annotation is carried out and is released to facilitate future benchmarking of dialog evaluation metrics

method.summary: Human annotation of 60 contexts per corpus (Topical-Chat, PersonaChat) on six qualities by six researchers, three per response. USR combines a RoBERTa-base masked-LM likelihood metric and two RoBERTa retrieval (true vs random reply) metrics through a regression fit to the human sub-quality-to-overall mapping, and is compared with 13 word-overlap and embedding metrics by turn- and system-level correlation.
method.task: automatic evaluation of open-domain dialog response generation

datasets.name: Topical-Chat
datasets.split: annotation: 60 dialog contexts randomly sampled from the frequent test set, 360 responses
datasets.preprocessing: heuristics identify the most relevant fact per response; MLM fine-tuned on dialog only, no facts

datasets.name: PersonaChat
datasets.split: annotation: 60 contexts from the ConvAI2 validation set, 300 responses
datasets.preprocessing: persona treated as analogous to Topical-Chat facts

models.name: Transformer (Topical-Chat response generator)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer, input is concatenation of context and fact
models.init_from: inferred: random (randomly-initialized word embeddings of size 300)

other.decoding: argmax and nucleus sampling p = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 (one model, four outputs)

other.note: a fourth model was excluded for possible data leakage

models.name: USR (RoBERTa-base sub-metrics + regression)
models.architecture: RoBERTa-base (Liu et al. 2019) fine-tuned for MLM, then for retrieval

training.objective: MLM metric: masked-LM on dialog; DR metric: binary classification of true vs randomly sampled response, as in Ubuntu dialog corpus; USR: regression from sub-metric scores to Overall Quality
training.epochs: RoBERTa MLM fine-tune: a single epoch; Transformer generator: 50 epochs; DR epochs not stated

other.mlm_fine_tune_data: training set of Topical-Chat, dialog only, via Wolf et al. 2019a implementation
other.regression: regression trained on z-scored human ratings, softmax over weights for Figure 2; trained per annotator for the analysis

inference.decoding: Transformer generator: argmax and nucleus sampling
inference.samples: one response per decoding strategy per context

metrics.name: Turn-level Spearman/Pearson
metrics.definition: correlation of metric score with human rating over individual responses (ground-truth annotations excluded)

metrics.name: MLM
metrics.definition: negative sum over response words of masked log-likelihood given context

metrics.name: DR
metrics.definition: P(y=1 | x, r) from retrieval classifier; x = c (history and fact) or x = f (fact only)

eval.protocol: Six dialog researchers, three annotators per response, randomly assigned; preliminary pass of 5 contexts each (30 responses) then instruction revision. Ratings: Understandable 0-1, Natural 1-3, Maintains Context 1-3, Interesting 1-3, Uses Knowledge 0-1, Overall Quality 1-5. Ground-truth annotations excluded from metric evaluation. Significance p<0.01 for Table 3 and Table 1; p>0.05 italicized in Tables 4-6.

evidence.quote: 60 dialog contexts randomly sampled from the frequent test set, for a total of 360 responses scored on six different qualities
The annotations for the original ground-truth are not used for evaluation

results.claim: USR turn-level correlation with Overall Quality on Topical-Chat.
results.setup: Topical-Chat, 60 contexts, reference-free responses of 5 non-ground-truth sources
results.note: Appendix Table 10 prints 0.4192 under the column headed Pearson and 0.4220 under Spearman; main Table 5 and abstract (0.42) say Spearman 0.4192.

results.note: Abstract/conclusion say 0.48, which matches USR-DR (x = c) 0.4814 in Table 6, not the USR row 0.4693; DR (x=c) outperforms USR here.

results.claim: System-level Spearman of USR with Overall Quality is 1.0 on both datasets.
results.n: 5 systems Topical-Chat, 4 PersonaChat (inferred from ground-truth exclusion)

results.quote: USR signiﬁcantly (p < 0.01) outperforms all other metrics with a Spearman correlation of 1.0 on both datasets and Pearson correlations of 0.92 (Topical-Chat) and 0.82 (PersonaChat).

USR should be used alongside human evaluation, not to claim superiority.
results.note: USR should not be used to claim superior performance over another method.

limits: Only 60 contexts per corpus, six researchers annotating, no crowdsourcing; Overall Quality annotations contain annotator-specific subjectivity.
System-level correlation rests on very few systems (inferred 5 on Topical-Chat, 4 on PersonaChat).
Best sub-metrics for each quality differ between datasets; on PersonaChat DR (x=c) alone beats USR.
May not work with non-generative models; responses from models similar to the evaluation models (e.g., DR) are a concern.
Nucleus sampling hyperparameters (e.g., temperature) not tuned; objective was varied quality, not best models.
Training hyperparameters of RoBERTa fine-tuning (optimizer, lr, batch size) and of the regression are not stated; list of baseline metrics is not exhaustive.
